subject: Re: MAP - tokenized economics gap analysis and eval gating
messages:
From: Alex Li <alex.li@medicore.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Gomez <m.gomez@medicore.com>
Date: 2028-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Cost model questions ahead of MAP kickoff

Evelyn — thanks again for the call this morning. Before we lock the MAP kickoff I want to make sure we have a shared view of the unit economics so procurement can sign off on the pilot. A few items the finance team flagged: 

- Tokens/$: your team referenced ~0.006 USD/token in the deck; that’s a big lever for us. Can you confirm what assumptions feed that number (sequence length, average tokens generated, quantization/throughput tier)?
- Caching/prefetching: we expect a decent fraction of requests to hit a cached prefix (clinical forms, templated responses). What hit-rate did you assume and how does that change tokens/$?
- Batching: our front-end can tolerate 250–350ms p95; how much batching can you run without breaching that?
- Evaluation plan: we need the MAP to include a clear gating metric (tokens per dollar + quality regression tolerance) and an experiment plan we can show procurement.

Attaching the draft MAP from our side (we’ll send a fuller requirements sheet after this). Appreciate a short reply with the high-level assumptions and a proposed pilot schedule.

—Alex
Medicore — Director, Product
attachments: medicore_requirements_v1.xlsx (ref)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Alex Li <alex.li@medicore.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-21T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cost model questions ahead of MAP kickoff

Alex — thanks for laying this out. Quick answers below and a proposed MAP fragment + eval gating attached (medicore_map_v2.xlsx). We should review live, but here is the distilled view so procurement has something to review immediately.

High-level unit-econ assumptions (pilot):
- Baseline request mix: average input 28 tokens, average model output 120 tokens => ~148 tokens total per request.
- Model variant: opt-quantized-ggml-v2 (16-bit quantization path in Dedicated).
- Pricing used: hosted pilot rate equivalence = $0.0009 per 100 tokens => ~0.0054 USD/token. This reflects batching and moderate cache reuse.

Caching/prefetch assumptions and sensitivity:
- Default MAP assumption: 40% cache hit on prefix + 10% KV reuse inside session => effective tokens emitted per request down by ~30% (to ~104 tokens).
- Scenarios provided in workbook: conservative (20% hit), expected (40% hit), optimistic (65% hit). Workbook shows tokens/$ and delta to baseline for each.

Batching vs latency (pilot constraints):
- With a p95 target of 250–350ms we recommend small micro-batches (batch sizes 4–8) with dynamic batching enabled; this yields ~12–18% cost reduction for generation-heavy calls while keeping p95 within target on Dedicated.
- If you can accept p95=500ms for non-interactive flows, we can push bigger batches (16–32) and double the batching savings.

Evaluation plan (short):
- Data collection window (2 weeks): supply representative production traces (we’ll need 10k sample requests).
- Simulations (2 days): Ben runs tokenization and batching simulations for the three cache-hit scenarios.
- Pilot (3 weeks): run on Dedicated with live traffic routing 10% -> Redwood; monitor tokens/day, cache hit-rate, latency p50/p95, and a quality metric (ROUGE/targeted prompts + manual spot checks).
- MAP gating: accept if tokens/$ under "expected" scenario <= $0.006 *and* quality regressions <= 2% on the eval set.

Action items / proposed timeline:
- Tomorrow: Ben to produce simulation workbook (conservative/expected/optimistic) — Ben, can you include a row-level sensitivity analysis for cache hit-rate?
- Wed 5/24: Laura to send final contract/PO gating checklist so procurement can map milestones.
- Fri 5/26: Final MAP doc synced; kickoff week of 5/29 if all good.

I attached the workbook with scenario tabs and a short runbook for the token model (token-model-runbook.pdf). If it helps, we can run a 1-day spike with a 70% cache-hit synthetic to show best-case economics.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 20m review with procurement if helpful.

Evelyn Hart
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
(e) evelyn.hart@redwood.com | (t) +1 415-555-0123
attachments: medicore_map_v2.xlsx, token-model-runbook.pdf

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-05-22T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Simulation asks for Medicore MAP (tokens/$)

Ben/Laura — copying the core asks from Medicore. Keeping this thread so we have the full trail. Please do not forward internal simulation outputs externally until we have a joint narrative.

Ben: deliverables
- Simulation workbook showing per-request token breakdown (prompt, generations, KV reuse) for conservative/expected/optimistic cache-hit rows. Include columns: avg_tokens/request, tokens_per_dollar, percent_cost_reduction vs baseline, and latency impact estimates at batch sizes [1,4,8,16].
- Run a synthetic run for a 70% cache-hit bucket as Evelyn offered; show best-case tokens/$ and how much of that depends on prefix vs intra-session KV reuse.
- Deadline: COB 5/24 so I can attach to MAP Friday.

Laura: deliverables
- Procurement gating checklist draft for Medicore (PO thresholds, acceptance testing, security paperwork deadlines).
- Confirm whether procurement will accept a 2-week data collection + 3-week pilot pipeline or needs a longer due-diligence window.
- Deadline: EOD 5/24.

Notes: keep the MAP gating clear: (1) econ: expected tokens/$ <= $0.006; (2) perf: p95 <= 350ms (interactive) or documented acceptance for non-interactive buckets; (3) quality: <=2% regression on eval prompts.

Evelyn

From: Maria Gomez <m.gomez@medicore.com>

Evelyn — thanks for the swift breakdown and the workbook. This reads well and aligns with what procurement needs. We reviewed the scenarios and have two quick asks before we finalize the MAP on Friday: 

1) Can Redwood provide the simulation workbook outputs for the 70% cache-hit synthetic (we saw you offered); procurement wants to see the sensitivity to prefix size and what fraction of the 70% is "exact prefix hit" vs "partial/KV reuse."
2) For the batching/latency tradeoffs: can you add a short column that maps batch size -> expected p99 tail (not just p95)? Our compliance team is specifically concerned about p99 for a small subset of critical workflows.

Assuming we get those two items by EOD Thursday we can approve the MAP and schedule the kickoff for week of 5/29. Also please share the final MAP link (Drive) in the thread so we have the canonical doc.

Thanks — Maria
VP Product, Medicore
